title: Minimum Score Triangulation of Polygon
summary: Given a convex polygon with integer values at each vertex, represented by an array values, the task is to divide the polygon into triangles such that the sum of the products of the vertex values in each triangle is minimized.
statement: Given a convex polygon with integer values at each vertex, represented by an array values, the task is to divide the polygon into triangles such that the sum of the products of the vertex values in each triangle is minimized. The polygon must be divided into exactly n - 2 triangles, where n is the number of vertices. Each triangle's weight is the product of its three vertices' values, and the goal is to find the minimum total score achievable through any valid triangulation.
constraints: At least three positive vertex values describe a convex polygon in order.
Minimize the sum of triangle vertex products.
hints: Every triangulation of interval i..j has one triangle using edge (i,j) and some middle k.
Use interval DP over increasing gaps.
Removing that boundary triangle splits the polygon into exactly the two independent subpolygons.
editorial: Removing that boundary triangle splits the polygon into exactly the two independent subpolygons.

tests.explanation: Choosing the diagonal between values three and four gives score 144.
